subject: humanities
passage: In 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an, China, struck fragments of a life-size clay soldier. Excavations soon revealed an army of thousands of such figures buried near the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of a unified China, who died in 210 BCE. Each of the soldiers, which stand in long rows facing east with their hands positioned to hold real weapons, ______ a slightly different face, and traces of paint show that they were once brightly colored.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the blank is "Each," which is always singular; "of the soldiers" and the long "which" clause only describe it. A singular subject takes the singular verb "has."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Are having" is plural; the subject "Each" is singular.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Having" is not a finite verb, so the clause would have no main verb at all.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Have" is plural and seems to agree with "soldiers," but the subject is the singular "Each."
explanation.D: Correct. The singular verb "has" agrees with the singular subject "Each."
